Space exploration won't be so nice for the future because it's not sustainable. Show less Read more Like 1 Dislike Reply @Alexis_lim 1 month ago Hello, we are students at Saint Joseph Reims, France and currently working on your video and have to make a comment that goes against your opinions. Just a heads up this is not hate. As you mentioned in your video, space exploration would improve and help us for our quality of life and sustainability. We're against that idea. Though current technologies allow us to go further, we think our priority consists to focus on real and actual problems such as water and food accessibility on Earth rather than space. Furthermore, the rockets launching use lots of fuel resulting in the release of greenhouse gases as well as pollution due to spaceship waste. Show less Read more Like 1 Dislike Reply @anisiamaniche4981 2 years ago Wow Show less Read more Like Dislike Reply @RaniaReama 1 month ago Great video! However, we think space exploration is just as dangerous as it is beneficial: this exploration of other planets and galaxies could lead to scientific breakthroughs. However it could also lead to the discovery of hostile new civilizations. Show less Read more Like Dislike Reply @tim40gabby25 3 years ago Spin offs are side effects - why not focus directly on Earth's problems, with maybe as exciting a payoff? Just asking. No! It’s about more than just sending people into space. It’s about pushing the boundaries of what’s possible, and using that knowledge to improve life on Earth. From developing new technologies that solve problems on Earth, to inspiring future generations to reach for the stars, the benefits of human space exploration are endless and closer than most may realize.
